name: The Modern Athonite Elders
dom: Hesychasm; monastic eldership; the Jesus Prayer
note: Hub for the modern Athonite startsy / gerontes (Mount Athos): Silouan, Joseph the Hesychast, Paisios, Porphyrios, who renewed hesychast prayer and spiritual fatherhood in the 20th c.

name: The Royal Martyrs (Romanov Passion-Bearers)
dom: Passion-bearing; new-martyrdom of the Russian Revolution
note: Collective hub for Tsar Nicholas II and his family, glorified in 2000 by the Moscow Patriarchate as passion-bearers (strastoterptsy) following their 1918 execution at Yekaterinburg.

name: Nikodemos the Hagiorite
dom: Hesychasm; spiritual anthology; canon law
note: Athonite monk (1749-1809), co-compiler of the Philokalia with Macarius of Corinth; foundational figure of the modern hesychast revival. Glorified 1955.

name: Ignatius Brianchaninov
dom: Asceticism; the Jesus Prayer; patristic spirituality
note: Russian bishop (1807-1867), author of The Arena and On the Prayer of Jesus; major modern systematizer of patristic ascetic teaching. Glorified 1988.

name: Theophan the Recluse
dom: Prayer of the heart; spiritual direction; Philokalic translation
note: Russian bishop (1815-1894) who retired into reclusion; translated the Philokalia into Russian (Dobrotolyubie) and wrote extensively on unceasing prayer. Glorified 1988.

name: John of Kronstadt
dom: Pastoral ministry; the Eucharist; healing; charity
note: Russian parish priest (1829-1908), famed wonderworker and author of My Life in Christ; renowned for frequent communion and miracles of healing. Glorified 1990.

name: Nektarios of Aegina
dom: Healing; humility under slander; monastic founding
note: Greek bishop (1846-1920), Metropolitan of Pentapolis, founder of the convent on Aegina; one of the most popular modern Greek wonderworkers and healers. Glorified 1961.

name: Silouan the Athonite
dom: Hesychasm; the Jesus Prayer; love of enemies; 'Keep your mind in hell'
note: Russian monk of St Panteleimon's Monastery on Athos (1866-1938); his life and teaching were transmitted by his disciple Sophrony. Glorified 1987.

name: Joseph the Hesychast
dom: Hesychasm; noetic prayer; Athonite monastic renewal
note: Athonite elder (1897-1959) whose disciples repopulated many Athonite monasteries; key figure in the 20th-c. hesychast revival. Glorified 2020.

name: Luke of Simferopol (Voino-Yasenetsky)
dom: Healing; medicine; confession under persecution
note: Russian archbishop and surgeon (1877-1961), Valentin Voino-Yasenetsky, confessor who suffered Soviet imprisonment and exile while practicing surgery. Glorified 1995/2000.

name: Matrona of Moscow
dom: Healing; clairvoyance; consolation under persecution
note: Blind Russian laywoman (1881-1952), Matrona Nikonova, venerated for healing and spiritual sight during the Soviet era; one of the most popular Russian saints. Glorified 1999/2004.

name: Elizabeth Feodorovna
dom: Charity; monastic foundation; new-martyrdom
note: Grand Duchess Elizabeth (1864-1918), founder of the Martha and Mary Convent; murdered by the Bolsheviks at Alapayevsk. New-martyr glorified 1981 (ROCOR) / 1992 (Moscow).

name: Tsar Nicholas II
dom: Passion-bearing; Christian rulership
note: Last Russian emperor (1868-1918), executed with his family at Yekaterinburg; glorified as a passion-bearer (strastoterpets) in 2000.

name: Empress Alexandra Feodorovna
dom: Passion-bearing
note: Last Russian empress (1872-1918), wife of Nicholas II; executed at Yekaterinburg and glorified as a passion-bearer in 2000.

name: Tsarevich Alexei
dom: Passion-bearing
note: Heir to the Russian throne (1904-1918), son of Nicholas II; executed at Yekaterinburg and glorified with his family as a passion-bearer in 2000.

name: John Maximovitch (of Shanghai and San Francisco)
dom: Healing; ascetic episcopate; diaspora mission
note: Russian Orthodox bishop (1896-1966) of the diaspora (Shanghai, Western Europe, San Francisco); ascetic wonderworker. Glorified 1994 (ROCOR).

name: Maria Skobtsova (Maria of Paris)
dom: Social charity; new-martyrdom; ministry to the persecuted
note: Russian emigre nun in Paris (1891-1945) who sheltered Jews and others under Nazi occupation; died at Ravensbruck. Glorified 2004 (Ecumenical Patriarchate).

name: Nikolai Velimirovic
dom: Preaching; theology; spiritual writing
note: Serbian bishop (1880-1956), 'the Serbian Chrysostom', author of the Prologue of Ohrid; imprisoned at Dachau. Glorified 2003 (Serbian Orthodox Church).

name: Justin Popovic
dom: Dogmatic theology; patristic revival; christocentric spirituality
note: Serbian theologian and archimandrite (1894-1979), author of the Dogmatics of the Orthodox Church and Lives of the Saints; disciple of patristic tradition. Glorified 2010.

name: Paisios of Mount Athos
dom: Spiritual counsel; the Jesus Prayer; discernment
note: Greek Athonite elder (1924-1994), among the most beloved modern startsy; renowned for counsel and discernment. Glorified 2015 (Ecumenical Patriarchate).

name: Porphyrios of Kavsokalyvia
dom: Clairvoyance; healing; spiritual counsel
note: Greek elder (1906-1991) of Kavsokalyvia on Athos and later Athens; famed for charismatic gifts of insight and healing. Glorified 2013 (Ecumenical Patriarchate).

name: Sophrony of Essex
dom: Hesychasm; the Jesus Prayer; monastic founding
note: Russian-born archimandrite (1896-1993), disciple and biographer of Silouan the Athonite; founder of the Monastery of St John the Baptist, Essex. Glorified 2019 (Ecumenical Patriarchate).
